heldout.unit_note: bits_per_encoded_token; 99.98% of tokens are single bytes, so this equals BPB to ~0.02%

bzip2_-9.verdict: statistical tie; floor lies inside the model 95% CI

generalization.note: Court IV predicted the gap would be small because the run consumes 19.6% of one epoch with no byte repeated. Confirmed: +0.0102 BPB.

court_iv_section_5_confirmation.verdict: The section 5 memory/transport trade is confirmed on trained weights, and is more severe than predicted. Section 5 projected a 2.1-token horizon at FULL transport; the model runs 38% of the transport cap and still averages a 1.72-token horizon. The denominator (1+|x|+|y|+|z|) accounts for 35.3% of all forgetting. The noncommutative term is genuinely in use -- relative central commutator 0.67 -- so the model is actively buying transport with memory, exactly the exchange section 5 identified.

contraction_certificate_confirmed.note: Court IV E1 proved ||qN||inf <= c_i sigma(a) < c_i < 1 analytically. The trained run's observed maximum is the slowest fiber's ceiling exp(-0.002) exactly, so the bound is tight and reached.

scan_parity_confirmed.note: Court IV E1 checked serial vs Hillis-Steele vs balanced tree agreement in float64 and found <= 2.7e-15. The run's own preflight finds exact 0.0 loss agreement across serial, reference and Triton on GPU.

caveat_contamination_check.assessment: This is a weak check. Distinct file digests prove only that the two files are not byte-identical; they do not establish that no held-out document also appears in training. The corpus metadata separately claims the split was made by source document, which if true is the real guarantee -- but this check does not verify it. A document-level hash intersection over the 257/258 delimiters would.
caveat_contamination_check.affects_headline_number: not materially, but the check should not be cited as proof of non-overlap
